slides.title: High-Flyer 56.6% Returns DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng’s quantitative
slides.text: High-Flyer 56.6% Returns DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng’s quantitative hedge fund generated returns of more than 50% last year https://x.com/business/status/2010632000382636056 https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-12/deepseek-founder-liang-s-funds-surge-57-as-china-quants-boom DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng's quantitative hedge fund, Zhejiang High-Flyer Asset Management, generated average returns of 56.6% across its funds in 2025, making it the second-best performer among Chinese quant funds managing over 10 billion yuan The fund abandoned market-neutral strategies in 2024 to go "all-in" on long-only strategies , which seek to beat underlying stock indexes rather than hedge positions - allowing to capture the full upside of China's stock market rally in 2025 High-Flyer Fund has been a pioneer in using AI for quantitative trading since its founding in 2015. The firm describes itself as fully relying on deep neural networks, with their first trade generated by a deep learning algorithm executed on October 21, 2016, and deep learning algorithms fully implemented for trading by 2017 High-Flyer's AI-driven approach automates every stage of operations—from data collection and analysis to portfolio construction and trade execution Their models process three main data sources: market data (price and volume indicators), macroeconomic fundamental data, and alternative data, all fed into neural networks to predict stock price changes The firm integrates machine learning and natural language processing to analyze massive datasets and financial behavior

slides.title: Cline - Skills, Background edits, Web Cline's Skills
slides.text: Cline - Skills, Background edits, Web Cline's Skills - modular instruction sets that load on-demand Skills help to reduce tokens usage VSCode Cline extension: Settings → Features → Enable Skills Click the scale icon below the chat input to access the rules and workflows panel, where you'll find a new Skills tab for managing your skills Each skill is a directory containing a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter and markdown instructions. The basic structure looks like this: my-skill/ ├── SKILL.md # Required: main instructions ├── docs/ # Optional: additional documentation │   └── advanced.md └── scripts/ # Optional: utility scripts └── helper.sh Your SKILL.md file needs two parts: the header (name and description) followed by the detailed instructions for Cline to follow. Example: --- name: my-skill description: Brief description - what it does, when to use it --- # My Skill Detailed instructions for Cline to follow ## Steps 1. First, do this 2. Then do that 3. For advanced usage, see advanced.md The "name" must exactly match the directory name, and the "description" (max 1024 characters) tells Cline when to activate this skill Skills can be stored in two locations: Global Skills for all projects: $HOME/.cline/skills/ Project Skills: .cline/skills/ or .clinerules/skills/ or .claude/skills/ for Claude Code compatibility The global skill takes precedence over local (strange) When your request matches a skill's description, Cline loads and activates it Skills tab in the rules and workflows panel - view all skills (global and workspace), toggle them on/off, create/delete skills Skills are useful for multi-step workflows or domain-specific knowledge, like Release management, Code review, Database migrations, API integration, Debugging workflows, Infrastructure Skills vs Rules vs Workflows: Rules - set constraints that are always active Workflows - explicit sequences you invoke with `/ workflow.md ` Skills - domain expertise, activated only when needed https://docs.cline.bot/features/skills https://cline.bot/blog/cline-3-48-0-skills-and-websearch-make-cline-smarter https://cline.ghost.io/cline-3-48-0-skills-and-websearch-make-cline-smarter/ Background Edits (enable in Settings → Features → Background Edits) allows Cline to work without opening diff views or stealing focus Cline can now search the web and pull page content directly. No browser, no screenshots. Useful when you need current docs or API references.

slides.title: HINDSIGHT Agent Memory System HINDSIGHT Agent Memory System
slides.text: HINDSIGHT Agent Memory System HINDSIGHT Agent Memory System https://medium.com/@tarangtattva2/a-new-agent-memory-system-just-dropped-and-it-finally-fixes-what-weve-been-getting-wrong-fc84589f75ca The HINDSIGHT agent memory system addresses a fundamental flaw in current AI agent memory: treating memory as simple text retrieval rather than meaningful understanding HINDSIGHT introduces four distinct memory networks: World Memory (objective facts), Experience Memory (agent's own actions), Opinion Memory (subjective beliefs with confidence scores), Observation Memory (neutral summaries) This separation prevents the confusion typical in systems that mix fact and opinion The system uses three core operations: Retain (converting conversations into coherent narratives preserving decision context), Recall (combining semantic search, keywords, graph traversal, and temporal filtering), Reflect (applying behavioral profiles like skepticism and empathy to generate responses). Crucially, opinions evolve with confidence scores that adjust based on new evidence On long-memory benchmarks, HINDSIGHT achieves 83% accuracy compared to 39% for traditional approaches, enabling agents that explain their reasoning, maintain stable preferences, and preserve personality across sessions

slides.text: Confucius SDK (Meta and Harvard) Confucius SDK, open source https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/01/09/meta-and-harvard-researchers-introduce-the-confucius-code-agent-cca-a-software-engineering-agent-that-can-operate-at-large-scale-codebases/ Meta and Harvard - Confucius Code Agent, open-source SOTA on benchmarks like SWE Bench Pro and SWE Bench Verified by prioritizing agent architecture over raw model size The Confucius SDK organizes around three design axes: - Agent Experience (context layout and working memory), - User Experience (readable traces and code diffs), - Developer Experience (observability and debugging) Implements three core mechanisms: - hierarchical working memory - partitions long context - a persistent note-taking system (cross-session learning) - modular tool extensions for file editing, command execution, and code search Claude 4.5 Sonnet + Confucius - outperforms Claude 4.5 Opus Rich tool handling - increases the resolve rate Cross-Session Learning (re-using notes between sessions) Meta-agent that automatically designs and tunes agent configurations through iterative build-test-improve loops

slides.title: Google Gemini "Buy" Button Google Universal Commerce Protocol
slides.text: Google Gemini "Buy" Button Google Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Gemini Buy Button Direct checkout capabilities in Gemini and AI Mode Search ("Buy" button) UCP - an open-source standard co-developed with Shopify, Walmart, Target, Wayfair, and Etsy UCP provides a unified language for AI agents to communicate with e-commerce systems - to find products and complete purchases for you It organizes these tasks into specific "capabilities," such as checking out or applying discounts, and keeps your financial information safe by using secure tokens rather than sharing your actual credit card details directly with every merchant Ultimately, UCP creates a secure bridge that allows AI to handle complex shopping errands across many different stores without needing custom integrations for each one UCP covers product search, payment processing, and post-purchase support, and has backing from over 20 companies including major payment processors (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, PayPal, Stripe) and retailers (Home Depot, Kroger, Lowe's, Gap) When users tap the "Buy" button, they can complete purchases with pre-filled payment methods (Google Pay, Google Wallet) and shipping information without leaving the AI conversation Business Agent - an AI virtual sales associate that appears as a "Chat" button in Search results for participating retailers like Lowe's, Michaels, Poshmark, and Reebok, capable of answering product questions in the brand's voice UCP directly competes with OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol and positions Google against OpenAI, Amazon, and Perplexity https://www.theverge.com/news/860446/google-ai-shopping-standard-buy-button-gemini https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/agentic-commerce-ai-tools-protocol-retailers-platforms/ https://apnews.com/article/google-gemini-ai-shopping-checkout-walmart-f1679240ba93d40b90a97348b73039d3

slides.title: Sakana AI Paper on Self-Improving AI Sakana AI
slides.text: Sakana AI Paper on Self-Improving AI Sakana AI Paper on Self-Improving AI New paper demonstrate recursively self-improving AI through a game called Core War, created in 1984 https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03335v1 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-EgTYDKtEw8 Core War is a programming game where players write assembly code for autonomous "warrior" programs that battle for control Sakana AI's "Digital Red Queen" (DRQ) algorithm uses LLMs in a self-play evolutionary loop where AI-generated warriors continuously battle each other without ever seeing human-created strategies. The name references the Red Queen Hypothesis from evolutionary biology , which states organisms must constantly evolve just to maintain survival against changing competitors After approximately 250 iterations of evolution, the AI-generated warriors beat human champions despite never encountering human strategies during training The LLMs independently discovered the same meta strategies humans took decades to develop, including effective bombing patterns and self-replication techniques Different AI runs showed convergent evolution, starting from completely different conditions but arriving at similar high performing behaviors The AI demonstrated an intuitive understanding of code lethality, predicting warrior effectiveness just by analyzing code without executing it This research demonstrates that AI improves faster through adversarial self-play in open-ended environments rather than memorizing textbooks The same approach could advance cybersecurity by discovering real-world computer viruses and defense mechanisms through self-play rather than training on existing threats Unlike previous AI game achievements (Chess, Go), Core War's Turing-complete environment represents unlimited strategic complexity more similar to real-world programming challenges The research is open-source on GitHub with visualizations available https://sakana.ai/drq/ https://www.linkedin.com/posts/sakana-ai_introducing-digital-red-queen-drq-adversarial-activity-7415218635578757120-esoB https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core_War

slides.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents Demystifying evals for
slides.text: Demystifying evals for AI agents Demystifying evals for AI agents - Anthropic Post https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents Effective evaluations are essential for shipping AI agents confidently - without them, teams get stuck fixing issues reactively in production Evals make problems visible before they affect users, with value that compounds over the agent lifecycle. An evaluation consists of: tasks (test cases), trials (repeated runs due to non-determinism), graders (scoring logic), transcripts (complete interaction records), outcomes (final environment state), evaluation harnesses (infrastructure running the tests) Three grader types are used: code-based (fast, objective, verifying specific conditions), model-based (flexible, handling nuanced judgments), human (authoritative but slow) Different agent types require tailored approaches. Coding agents use deterministic tests like unit tests. Conversational agents need multidimensional rubrics covering task completion and interaction quality. Research agents combine groundedness checks, coverage verification, and source quality assessment. Computer use agents verify outcomes in sandboxed GUI environments. Teams should start early with 20-50 real-world failure cases, write unambiguous tasks with reference solutions, build balanced problem sets, design robust harnesses with stable environments, and continuously read transcripts to validate graders. Evals work best alongside production monitoring, A/B testing, and user feedback for a complete performance picture.

slides.text: AI Updates Meta Nuclear Power for AI Meta signed nuclear power agreements with TerraPower, Oklo, and Vistra to supply up to 6.6 gigawatts of power by 2035 These deals will support Meta's Prometheus AI data center in New Albany, Ohio, which is planned as a 1-gigawatt cluster anticipated to come online in 2026 The Vistra agreement is a 20-year deal providing over 2.1 gigawatts from existing nuclear plants in Ohio (Perry and Davis-Besse) and Pennsylvania (Beaver Valley), plus an additional 433 megawatts from planned upgrades The TerraPower partnership will fund development of two Natrium sodium fast reactors delivering up to 690 megawatts starting in 2032, with rights to six additional units providing 2.1 gigawatts by 2035. The Oklo agreement supports development of a 1.2-gigawatt power campus in Pike County, Ohio, with the first phase targeting 2030 and full capacity by 2034 These agreements make Meta one of the largest corporate nuclear energy buyers in U.S. history https://www.utilitydive.com/news/meta-nuclear-deal-oklo-vistra-terrapower-ai-data-centers/809215/ https://www.cbsnews.com/news/meta-nuclear-power-deals-ai-data-centers/ https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/09/meta-signs-deals-with-three-nuclear-companies-for-6-plus-gw-of-power/ DeepSeek V4 planned mid-February around Chinese New Year V4 focuses specifically on coding capabilities The model particularly excels at handling extremely long coding prompts and maintaining logical consistency across complex software engineering tasks There are also indications that V4 may integrate reasoning capabilities previously associated with a rumored DeepSeek R2 model, enabling more efficient logical processing alongside code generation https://www.theverge.com/news/859564/deepseek-is-reportedly-close-to-releasing-a-flagship-ai-model-that-outperforms-claude-and-chatgpt-in-coding https://www.reuters.com/technology/deepseek-launch-new-ai-model-focused-coding-february-information-reports-2026-01-09/

slides.title: AI Updates Unlock "Infinite" AI Memory With Claude
slides.text: AI Updates Unlock "Infinite" AI Memory With Claude Code https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-uwnpmziGA Idea - keep memory externally. 3 files: Context File - primary goal To-Dos File - track progress (check list) Insights File - output Claude Co-Work - a Desktop AI agent that works with your files Currently only available in a Mac desktop app for Claude Max plan subscribers https://claude.com/download It allows Claude to work autonomously on complex tasks using your local files, web browsing, and extended reasoning capabilities. You can describe a complex task, give it access to a folder on your computer, and step away while it independently plans and executes multi-step work Cowork can read, modify, and generate local files without manual uploads, create professional outputs like Excel spreadsheets with formulas and PowerPoint presentations, and coordinate multiple parallel workstreams for complex tasks Cowork built into the Claude Desktop app for macOS . It runs in an isolated environment on your desktop and provides progress indicators so you can monitor or steer the work mid-task https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-getting-started-with-cowork https://venturebeat.com/technology/anthropic-launches-cowork-a-claude-desktop-agent-that-works-in-your-files-no

slides.text: AI Updates MiroThinker v1.5 Deep Research Open-source AI research agent 256K token context window, up to 400 tool calls per task 30B and 235B params Uses cyclical "think–act–observe" process where the model analyzes situations, invokes tools, receives results, and updates its understanding until tasks are solved The system acts as a "scientist" by executing a "slow-thinking" research loop: proposing hypotheses, querying external data for evidence, discovering mismatches, revising hypotheses, and verifying until evidence converges It can perform future trend forecasting by evaluating chain reactions of macro events, enabling proactive decision-making rather than just summarizing historical data https://github.com/MiroMindAI/MiroThinker https://huggingface.co/miromind-ai/MiroThinker-v1.5-30B https://dr.miromind.ai - interactive demo MIT's new Adaptive Radix Tree (ART) Modern NVMe SSDs eliminated disk I/O bottlenecks, making RAM-to-cache communication the new constraint ART 3.2x faster than B-trees on read-heavy workloads B-trees still won on write-heavy workloads (18% faster inserts) Neither structure universally "wins"—they fit different use cases Both structures struggle with skewed, real-world key distributions. https://medium.com/@speedcraft21/mit-just-killed-b-trees-i-spent-2-weeks-proving-theyre-right-and-wrong-467a6f3964e7 Merge Labs raised 252 Mln Co-founded by Sam Altman Building devices to connect human brains to computers BCI = brain-computer interface (BCI) https://merge.io/blog

slides.title: Why Memory Prices Are So High? Why computer
slides.text: Why Memory Prices Are So High? Why computer memory prices are so high? DDR5 prices surging more than 260% across major markets since September 2025 Primary reason - memory producers shifting capacity from consumer DRAM to HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) for AI datacenters HBM manufacturing is far more complex than standard DRAM, involving stacking 12 to 16 layers of memory onto a single chip to create a "cube" structure that can deliver the terabytes-per-second bandwidth AI chips require. One layer - 30 micron. So 16 layers is 0.48 mm  thick. Major memory makers have prioritized orders from hyperscalers and OEMs building AI servers, leaving less DRAM available for smartphones, PCs, and other consumer devices Samsung reportedly doubled the contract price for DDR5 to RAM manufacturers in December 2025, and industry analysts warn that a standard 32GB DDR5 module could exceed $500 by mid-2026 https://www.idc.com/resource-center/blog/global-memory-shortage-crisis-market-analysis-and-the-potential-impact-on-the-smartphone-and-pc-markets-in-2026/

slides.text: Nvidia StarCloud-1 Satellite StarCloud - training AI Model in Space StarCloud, backed by Nvidia, achieved a historic first by training an AI model in space aboard its StarCloud-1 satellite Launched in November 2025 on a SpaceX Falcon 9, the 130-pound satellite carries an Nvidia H100 GPU—100 times more powerful than any previous space GPU The satellite successfully trained nanoGPT on Shakespeare's works and runs Google's Gemma language model for live inference, proving transformers can operate in vacuum and radiation StarCloud plans 5-GWatt orbital data centers with 4-kilometer solar and cooling panels StarCloud-2 launches October 2026 with multiple H100s and Blackwell B200 chips - wildfire detection, satellite imagery Competition intensifies: Google's Project Suncatcher targets 2027, Jeff Bezos predicts gigawatt space data centers in 10+ years, and Eric Schmidt acquired Relativity Space for orbital infrastructure https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/10/nvidia-backed-starcloud-trains-first-ai-model-in-space-orbital-data-centers.html https://www.geekwire.com/2025/starcloud-power-training-ai-space/ https://introl.com/blog/orbital-data-centers-space-ai-infrastructure-guide-2025 https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/starcloud/

slides.title: Jobs - Demand for AI Engineer AI engineers
slides.text: Jobs - Demand for AI Engineer AI engineers build applications using existing AI models rather than creating models from scratch The current job market has over 500,000 open AI and ML engineering roles globally. Most of these roles require people who can build LLM-powered applications AI engineers earn a median salary of approximately $242,000 annually, with senior positions at companies like OpenAI earning over $700,000 AI-related job postings increase. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects 26% growth through 2033. 40% of the most in-demand AI skills don't yet exist in the current workforce The most in-demand technical skills include Python, prompt engineering, RAG, LangChain, vector databases, and cloud platforms https://www.coursera.org/articles/ai-engineer-salary https://www.roberthalf.com/us/en/job-details/aiml-engineer How to become an AI Engineer: Phase 1: Fundamentals (1.5-3 months) - Python, data structures, APIs, JSON, and error handling. Git and GitHub. Basic machine learning concepts (models, training vs. inference, embeddings) Phase 2: LLM Integration (2-3 months) - prompt engineering (system prompts, few-shot learning, chain-of-thought prompting), work with AI APIs from OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-source options through Hugging Face. Token management, cost control, response handling Phase 3: Building AI Systems (2-3 months) - LangChain framework for building LLM application pipelines. RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation), vector DBs. AI agents - querying databases, calling APIs, triggering workflows. Model Context Protocol (MCP) for connecting AI to external tools and services. Basic LLM ops (prompt versioning, monitoring, cost management) Phase 4: Job Preparation (ongoing) - build portfolio projects demonstrating key skills: an AI decision support system using RAG with citations and confidence scores; a natural language analytics system connecting LLMs to SQL databases; and an AI workflow orchestrator with agents and API integration

slides.text: Sam Altman - Best Time Ever Sam Altman - best time ever to start a new career (2024) https://x.com/StartupArchive_/status/2010396665199403341 Sam Altman: “This is probably the best time (maybe ever) to be starting your career” When asked how startup founders should handle a failed venture or pivot, Sam responds: “First of all, I think this is probably the best time — maybe ever — to be starting out your career because you will get to surf the greatest technological wave, maybe ever. And what that means is you can change course many times because you will have this unbelievable tailwind.” He advises founders to not get too hung up on any particular setback or failure — or even just changing your mind if you find something more exciting to go after: “I think this is going to be an unusual time in how much it rewards adaptability and decisive and quick movement. And I would trust that… And not get hung up on the fact that you decided to pivot or something didn’t work because you are just going to be flooded with opportunities for the next few years.” He concludes: “It’s still hard. It still always feels like a setback. But take the time you need to go on vacation, go for a hike, or just stew over it for a little while. But when you get back up, get back up with vigor.” Google’s Sergey Brin admits he’s hiring ‘tons’ of workers without degrees: ‘They just figure things out on their own in some weird corner’ https://finance.yahoo.com/news/google-sergey-brin-admits-hiring-170658486.html Engineers who get promoted quickly proactively identify and solve business problems before they become formal projects. Instead of waiting for work to be assigned to them, they build relationships with people outside engineering - product managers, customer support, sales, and finance - and consistently ask "What's hard right now?". They then solve these problems independently, creating demonstrable organizational impact beyond just executing assigned roadmap items. The key insight is that promotion comes from solving problems others care about, not from writing better code or working harder on assigned tasks. ​ https://levelup.gitconnected.com/i-studied-50-engineers-who-got-promoted-fast-they-all-did-one-thing-id-been-ignoring-f251cc99908b
